speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I see you're experiencing dizziness, nausea, and imbalance. To help me understand your condition better, have these symptoms been constant or do they come and go? And do you feel any hearing changes or ringing in your ears?

speaker: Patient
text: 27-year-old male. The patient reports a sustained sensation of the room spinning since this morning, which is low grade and constant. He occasionally feels nauseous and has taken diphenhydramine to help him sleep, which also alleviates his symptoms slightly. He mentions recent increased intake of garlic due to trying to recover from a cold a few days ago. Past medical history is unremarkable.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That's helpful; please tell me, did you experience any hearing loss, tinnitus, or visual disturbances when the dizziness started? Also, have you noticed any weakness, numbness, or difficulty speaking?

REQUEST TEST: Audiometry, CT Head with contrast.

REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Brain (post-contrast), MRI Vestibular Nerves.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Multiple sclerosis

REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with and without contrast.
REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Brain axial, coronal, and sagittal views.

Why did I mention these specific tests? Because the combination of persistent vertigo, nausea, and your recent garlic intake raises concern for a central nervous system issue rather than a common inner ear infection. We need to rule out demyelinating lesions in the brainstem or cerebellum to confirm the diagnosis.
